question.text: The contract value for cross-currency futures is denominated in:

answer.text: The quote currency of the pair (e.g., USD for EURUSD, JPY for USDJPY)
The base currency of the pair

explanation.text: The Logic: A cross-currency futures contract value is computed as trade price multiplied by the lot size of 1000, expressed in the quote currency of the pair. EURUSD and GBPUSD contract values are in USD, while USDJPY contract values are in JPY. For margin purposes the quote-currency value is converted to INR using FBIL reference rates, and cross-currency derivative margins are collected in INR. The Trap: Although margin collection happens in INR, the contract value itself is naturally in the quote currency of the pair, not in INR or the base currency. Note: Workbook references — pp.57 and 59 (cross-currency contract value = trade price x 1000 in quote currency; EURUSD/GBPUSD in USD, USDJPY in JPY; INR conversion via FBIL), pp.174 and 176 (INR collection for cross-currency derivative margins).
